study type: retrospective dual-center study (model development and external validation)
cohort: The study included 257 pregnant women with comorbid gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) from electronic medical records, split into development (n=121) and external validation (n=136) cohorts.
finding: The Naive Bayes model demonstrated robust predictive ability and interpretability for identifying preterm birth risk in pregnancies with comorbid GDM and HDP, achieving an AUC of 0.777 in the external validation cohort.
gest_age: The study focused on predicting preterm birth (birth before 37 weeks of gestation), and one key predictor, systolic blood pressure, was measured at 32-36 weeks.
